Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. The players are out in the middle. Fakhar Zaman and Haseebullah Khan to open for Pakistan. Pramod Madushan to bowl first.
... The Run Chase ...

Pakistan will look to wrap up the series with a clean sweep, while Sri Lanka aims to salvage some pride. The pitch has been unpredictable, and the Lankan bowlers will need to attack the stumps and vary their pace to trouble the Pakistani batters. Can Sri Lanka defend their total and salvage some pride, or will Pakistan chase it down and inflict a clean sweep? Let's find out.

Pakistan's bowling was top-notch as they dug deep and restricted Sri Lanka to 211, thanks to some brilliant performances. Mohammad Wasim was on fire, taking 3 wickets, while Haris Rauf and Faisal Akram claimed 2 each. Faheem Ashraf and Shaheen Afridi added to the tally with 1 wicket each. A flawless bowling display from the Men in Green!

Sri Lanka's batting struggles persist, as they failed to capitalise on their promising start, scoring 57 in the first 10 overs, only to be bowled out for 211 in the 46th over. Sadeera Samarawickrama's 48 was the top score, with others contributing, but the lack of a big score from one or two has left them in a difficult position. The visitors' inability to convert starts into big scores remains a concern, and it's a trend that's unchanged even after this ODI.

Another poor show with the bat for Sri Lanka as they're all out for 211, and it's a disappointing end to their innings as they have been bowled out in 46 overs. The openers gave them a great start, but the rest of the batting unit failed to capitalise, getting in and out at the wrong time.
